title: Toronto four-storey single-exit residential feasibility case study
code_edition: 2012 Ontario Building Code (City page identifies the consultant report baseline); exact amendment set is not stated in the study
document_date: 2024-06-25 consultant report; City staff report dated 2024-06-26

facts.text: The City-commissioned report studies a specific four-storey residential case-study building with one exit stair.
The report explicitly says it does not produce an alternative solution; it is intended to identify factors that may support or preclude a future proposal.
Potential measures discussed include sprinklers, caps on suites/area/occupants and travel distance, occupancy limits, a wider stair, and enhanced corridor or stair protection.
The report cautions that sprinkler or corridor upgrades may not address every emergency that could require rapid evacuation and says further stakeholder review is needed for some risks.

limitations: This is a City-commissioned feasibility study, not an actual permit application or approved alternative solution.
The report contains no identifiable owner, site, application number, or permit drawings.
Toronto’s public-facing page states the study used the 2012 OBC and is not a guarantee of approval under the later code.
